agreement_words: Agreement is not a forecast. This board shows only where separate families of readings point the same way, in each family's own words. It adds no prediction, no score and no call of its own: readings agreeing with each other says nothing by itself about what a price does next.
counted_words: Names that are not listed are counted above, not listed as agreement: a name is listed only when two or more families that carry a direction speak for it and every direction word agrees. The filings, facts and news families report figures and headlines only, with no direction word of their own, and the per-name prints record carries no judged direction either, so a name covered by several families can still carry only one direction, or none, and there is no second direction for it to agree with.
coverage_words: 1,838 names are on record for Tuesday, November 3, 2026: 22 by 5 families, 23 by 4 families, 5 by 3 families, 53 by 2 families, 1,730 by 1 family, and 5 by none. Only 0 names have two or more families that carry a direction pointing the same way.
proving_note: The tool only reports, filters, calculates or counts from records on file; it makes no forecast claim of its own, so there is nothing to grade.
proving_state: A measuring tool, nothing to prove

ruling_words: The research record has already ruled on a claim like this one. The claim: "A chart ranker's 0.736 ranking agreement is a forecasting result." The grading: Did not hold up. Ruled not a prediction: the 0.736 measures agreement with one fitted 55-name vendor snapshot, not agreement with future returns, and it was reached only after three rotation mistakes and a split-adjustment fault in the ranker's data were corrected. Checked against: One fitted snapshot of 55 names from the vendor. This board is built to that ruling: agreement is shown as agreement, and nothing more.

zero_words: No name on the record for this trading day has two or more families that carry a direction pointing the same way, so the board is empty for this day. The families were read and counted above; none of them agreed. An empty board is this day's true picture, not a missing one.
